summaries.summary: DNN are widely used in industry for NLP tasks such as text classification, sequence labeling, and question answering, but engineers face challenges applying them.
The challenges hinder engineer productivity and yield less optimal solutions, motivating an NLP toolkit for DNN models and a survey identifying three typical personas.
The NLP toolkit must be generic and flexible; analysis of a commercial centralized GPU cluster found about 87.5% NLP related jobs in common tasks and more than 90% of networks used common components.
NeuronBlocks was developed as a DNN toolkit for NLP tasks with an upper layer of end-to-end network templates and a bottom layer of reusable standard components.
The technical contributions of NeuronBlocks are summarized into three aspects.
General-purpose deep learning frameworks such as TensorFlow, PyTorch and Keras offer flexibility and support NLP tasks, but require large overhead to master framework details.
OpenNMT targets neural machine translation or other natural language generation tasks, while AllenNLP provides pre-built models, but both are limited to certain tasks and insufficiently flexible.
Neuronblocks is built on PyTorch and consists of the Block Zoo and Model Zoo, with reusable blocks and JSON configuration templates enabling task completion without coding efforts.
The Block Zoo recognizes major functional categories of neural network components, covers commonly used modules, and is open for future modules.
The paragraph contains item formatting settings: [itemsep= -0.4em,topsep = 0.3em, align=left, labelsep=-0.6em, leftmargin=1.2em].
The Embedding Layer supports Word/character embedding and extra handcrafted feature embedding such as pos-tagging.
Neural Network Layers include RNN, CNN, QRNN BIBREF2, Transformer BIBREF3, Highway network, Encoder Decoder architecture, attention layers, and regularization layers.
Besides loss functions built in PyTorch, the Block Zoo offers more options such as Focal Loss BIBREF6.
Supported Metrics include AUC, Accuracy, Precision/Recall, F1, F1/Accuracy, MSE/RMSE, and ExactMatch/F1 for classification, sequence labeling, knowledge distillation, and MRC tasks.
NeuronBlocks identifies four types of most popular NLP tasks and provides various end-to-end network templates for each task.
Text Classification and Matching supports tasks such as domain/intent classification and question answer matching.
Sequence Labeling predicts each token in a sequence into predefined types, with common tasks including NER, POS tagging, and Slot tagging.
NeuronBlocks provides a knowledge distillation template to improve inference speed of heavy DNN models like BERT/GPT.
Extractive Machine Reading Comprehension predicts the start and end positions of answer spans in a passage given a question and passage pair.
NeuronBlocks provides a convenient user interface for users to build, train, and test DNN models.
The I/O interface defines model input/output, such as training data, pre-trained models/embeddings, and model saving path.
The Model Architecture interface is the key configuration file part defining the whole model architecture as a list of layers/blocks from the Block Zoo.
The Training Parameters interface indicates the model optimizer and all other training hyper parameters.
Users write a JSON configuration file to instantiate Model Zoo templates or construct architectures from Block Zoo blocks, with shared configuration across training, test, and prediction.
Experiments on CoNLL-2003 BIBREF14, GLUE benchmark BIBREF13, and WikiQA corpus BIBREF15 showed NeuronBlocks models achieved reliable, competitive results with productivity greatly improved.
On CoNLL-2003 BIBREF14 English NER, NeuronBlocks used BIOES and 12 layer/block combinations, easily reproducing original model performance with comparative or slightly better performance.
On the GLUE benchmark BIBREF13, BiLSTM and Attention based models built by NeuronBlocks achieved competitive or even better results with minimal coding efforts.

On Domain Classification Dataset, AUC and QPS showed the student model by NeuronBlocks achieved 23-27 times inference speedup with only small performance regression compared with BERTbase fine-tuned classifier.

WikiQA corpus BIBREF15 contains 3,047 questions from Bing query logs, and CNN, BiLSTM, and Attention based models in NeuronBlocks achieved competitive or even better results with simple model configurations.

NeuronBlocks is a PyTorch DNN toolkit for NLP tasks with a two-layer solution balancing generality and flexibility, verified by extensive experiments and widely used in a commercial search engine product team.
As an open-source toolkit, NeuronBlocks will be further extended in various directions, with a few examples named below.
